questions.question: What does "show, don't tell" mean in creative writing?
options: Describe through actions and details rather than stating emotions directly
Use pictures instead of words
Show your work to others beføre publishing
Tell the story in chronological order
questions.explanation: Instead of writing "She was nervous," you show it: "Her hands trembled as she reached for the door handle." This creates more vivid, engaging writing.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a short story and a novel?
options: A short story focuses on one main event with limited characters
A short story has more characters
A short story has multiple subplots
There is no difference except length
questions.explanation: Short stories are focused and compact, typically centering on a single conflict or event with a small cast of characters.

questions.question: Which type of conflict involves a character struggling with their own feelings or decisions?
options: Person vs. Self
Person vs. Person
Person vs. Nature
Person vs. Society
questions.explanation: Internal conflict (Person vs. Self) involves a character's inner struggles with emotions, decisions, or moral dilemmas.

questions.question: What makes a good opening line for a story?
options: It creates questions and makes the reader want to continue
It describes the weather in detail
It introduces every character
It explains the entire plot
questions.explanation: Effective opening lines hook readers by raising questions, creating tension, or suggesting something unusual that compels them to read on.

questions.question: When writing dialogue, why should you add action between speeches?
options: To avoid "talking heads" and show what characters are doing
To make the story longer
To fill space on the page
To confuse the reader
questions.explanation: Adding action makes dialogue feel more natural and shows character behavior, making scenes more visual and engaging.
